title: IELTS Listening Part 1 Information-Point Blueprint
description: Ten information points with turn anchors and question-type grouping. Delivered alongside material.json for reviewer annotation display. MUST NOT be given to the audit step, which builds its own map blind.

split_after.description: Last item number of the first question group; must match the narrator's stated ranges.

question_type_coverage.description: Item numbers grouped by question type. Flattened, must equal exactly 1..10 with no repeats. Redundant with items[].item_form by design: this view supports auditing overall type distribution, the per-item field supports rendering each annotation.

correction.description: One self-correction where a final value cancels an earlier value. Order in script must be earlier -> marker -> final.

indirect_confirmation.description: Optional. The paraphrase/indirect-reference cycle, when the material uses one. Measured over the 27 usable archived papers: only 4 contain an indirect reference, while 24 use 先说后改 and 21 use a qualifier. The spec asks for 2-3 distraction cycles chosen from five mechanisms (§4B-4), not for this specific one, so requiring it made the generator chase a convention the real papers rarely follow.

type.description: Detail type per spec 4B-3. At least four distinct types required across the ten items.

target.description: The recordable value. Must occur inside evidence.

evidence.description: Shortest sufficient quote from the dialogue turn carrying this point.

turn_index.description: Index into material.json turns array. Anchors the annotation for marginal display. Must point at a non-speaker1 turn whose text contains evidence. Revision MUST keep this in sync -- a stale anchor shows reviewers an annotation beside the wrong sentence, which is very hard to detect downstream.

item_form.description: Question type this point can support.

form_group.description: Points sharing a form_group can combine into one table/form question. null means a standalone gap-fill. At least one group of >=3 points is required so the material can actually support a table or form question.

distractor.description: Part of a deliberate distractor cycle. Must be a complete census, not selected examples: 2-3 true across the ten items.

confirmed.description: Repeated or confirmed in dialogue. >=3 required; spelling and numeric points must be confirmed since they are the easiest to mishear under once-only listening.
